Fig. 36 shows the nano-scale microstructure comparison of the two alloys, which the aspect ratio of the HS4-T6 alloys is higher than that of HS2-T6. For the HS2-T6 alloy, 20 TEM images have been taken are analyzed by a MATLAB code at Ford where the images of Al-channel are binarized and the nanoparticles are analyzed. The average volume fraction of the particles of HS2-T6 is calculated to be 1.44% and average particle aspect ratio is 1.69±0.62 with median value to be 1.50. The average volume fraction of the particles of HS4-T6 is calculated to be 1.58% and average particle aspect ratio is 2.09±0.84 with median value to be 1.93. Mechanical test 4.5.2.1 Tensile test Apart from the HS2-T6 alloy, the HS2-T4 temper and HS4-T6 and T4 temper alloys are studied in this work. 9 tensile tests are performed for each of these samples and the average flow curves of the alloys are as shown in Fig. 38. As expected, the T4 alloys have lower yield stress, but larger working rate and HS4 alloys are in general stronger than the HS2 alloys, 35 Fig. 38. The average flow curve of each alloy calculated from tension tests. 4.5.2.2 Bending test results and macro-simulations Fig. 39 shows the bending test results of the 4 alloys. As is noted from the HS2-T6 alloys, the flow curves needs to be modified from that of tensile tests. Using the modified flow curves, the load-displacements of the macro-simulation fit well with those of the experiments.
